An example of your elitism includes your belief that all those who hold religious beliefs are simply not approaching it rationally.

I disagree that people don't examine their own religion objectively. When comparing religions, I think most people who are reasonable will use the logic of their own beliefs to disagree with others' faiths.

For example, followers of one major faith believe that their central figure was truly divine and that through their sacrifice, they opened the way to salvation for all humanity. They do not revere figures from other religions because they hold their own beliefs as the truth. They believe in their central figure's divinity because of the miracles attributed to them, such as transforming water into wine and performing other extraordinary acts. Therefore, they see their central figure as both human and divine, which supports their belief in their faith. This is a logical argument made within the context of religion to favor one belief over another. Does it mean that it is definitively correct? No, but it is a valid argument.

In summary, your perception of contemporary religious individuals seems to be that of an elderly person who is quick to judge anyone who disagrees. Most people of your generation who adhere to some form of organized faith are generally open to the existence of other religions and use events or beliefs from their own faith to support their convictions. It's not about disproving other religions.
